A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimulCost benchmark and toolkit. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support comparison, including matching relocated material. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations across 12 simulators, with success rates, computational costs, optimization comparisons, ablations, and failure analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds CGYRO results, additional optimizer comparisons, prompt sensitivity experiments, failure-inclusive cost analysis, and a tool-augmented tuning ablation.

M1.justification: Appendix C.8 introduces an evaluated inference variant in which an LLM supplies an initial guess and programmatic brute-force search performs refinement. v1 discussed callable search as future work. The original single-round and multi-round procedures and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 extends existing plasma-physics coverage with linear CGYRO simulations involving gyrokinetic eigenmodes and 12 plasma profiles. It adds 31 tasks per inference mode, increasing totals from 2,916/1,900 to 2,947/1,931. The original 12 simulators remain represented.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's scanning and BO-GP comparisons, v2 C.6 evaluates Bisection and Nelder-Mead 1D against scanning and reports limited (1+1)-ES trials. This substantially broadens the classical optimizer comparisons. EPOCH disappears from the BO success-rate comparison in Table 18, although its efficiency comparison remains in Table 19.

E3.justification: v2 adds an unconditional cost metric including failures, a 25-variant prompt evaluation, and CGYRO eigenvalue thresholds of 10^-3, 10^-4, and 10^-5 with fixed-hardware timing. Existing LLM budgets and temperatures remain unchanged. Section 4.6 narrows the stated BO scope to 11 solvers, inconsistently retaining EPOCH in the efficiency table.

E4.justification: New Appendices C.6–C.8 test the adequacy of scanning against alternative optimizers, sensitivity to prompt wording, the effect of including failed-run costs, and whether LLM initialization accelerates programmatic search. Two Euler 1D examples examine expensive conservative guesses. Existing ICL, reasoning-effort, and failure-mode analyses are retained.

E5.justification: C.7.1 introduces Spearman rank-correlation analysis comparing conditional efficiency with inverse unconditional cost. Existing McNemar tests, mixed-effects regression, FDR correction, and Fisher-z procedures remain. Updated statistical values and additional regression rows are result changes; no increased repeated-run count or new seed protocol is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds CGYRO results and the optimizer, unconditional-cost, prompt-sensitivity, and hybrid-search outcomes in Tables 13–17. Table 16 reports a success-rate change of +0.086 and efficiency change of -0.520. GPT-5 aggregate success changes from 63.8%/80.3% to 65.0%/81.1%, but coverage differs, so this is not a same-setting improvement. Original per-solver scores largely remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds the gyrokinetic evolution equation and strong-magnetization and scale-separation assumptions underlying CGYRO, with a restriction to linear simulations. This extends the formal physics specification. Existing mathematical formulations and search algorithms are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central cost-aware benchmarking contribution and conclusions about unreliable initial guesses and costly LLM refinement remain. Claimed coverage expands to 13 simulators, and Section 6 adds a recommendation to use intermediate initial parameter values when combining LLM guesses with search.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking hybrid-search overhead to conservative guesses, Nelder-Mead overhead to adjacent evaluations and cache misses, and unconditional multi-round costs to failed attempts. Section 6 adds qualifications about evaluating novel scientific tasks and handling non-monotonic parameters. The principal interpretations of ICL, reasoning effort, and transfer remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents CGYRO's discretization, six tunable parameters, plasma-profile construction, convergence checks, implementation source, and use of the specified machine for timing. C.6 describes discretized-grid Bisection and log-space Nelder-Mead. Existing LLM settings, BO hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and main repository information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Candy et al. (2016) for CGYRO and positions it as another production simulation code. Most other reference edits update bibliographic metadata or publication venues for existing works. The benchmark's central positioning around neglected tool costs remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the extensive prompt and failure-log appendix are retained. v2 expands Sections 4.7 and 6, inserts appendix subsections, adds acknowledgments and an impact statement, and removes visible Yang draft annotations. Running headers become the placeholder 'Title Suppressed Due to Excessive Size'.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised to incorporate CGYRO, five new tables present supplementary studies, and existing tables gain CGYRO entries. Figures and tables undergo local relocation and reflow. Figures 2–8 themselves are unchanged, despite updates to several corresponding numerical tables and passages.

improvement.justification: The new failure-inclusive cost analysis, alternative optimizers, and LLM-initialized-search ablation address gaps in v1's deployment evidence; CGYRO adds production-code coverage. These benefits are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Figure 2 retains old values despite updated Tables 4–5, and Table 14 contradicts the claim that only GPT-OSS has multi-round relative cost below 1. The revision provides useful additional evidence but needs reconciliation of its reporting.
